sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Dakota County, Minnesota?
sections.html:
Deeds, mortgages and liens are recorded at the Property Taxation & Records office in the Administration Center at 1590 Highway 55 in Hastings. The county says documents are accepted for recording only at that office, either by appointment or by mail.

For questions call 651-438-4597 or write to records@co.dakota.mn.us. For a mailed filing, send the documents and fees to Attn: Document Recording, with a cover letter describing what is enclosed, a self-addressed stamped envelope and a phone number. Originals come back to the sender in one to two weeks.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Dakota County?
sections.html:
Dakota County says every recording fee is set by the state, and that the $46 for indexing and recording a deed or other instrument comes from Minnesota Statutes section 357.18. That statute splits the $46 into $10.50 for the state general fund, $10 for the county technology fund and $25.50 for the county general fund. Fees are due when you file.

Dakota County recorder fees and transfer taxes (Property Taxation and Records filing fee page)
ItemAmount
Abstract document or Torrens memorial$46
Plat or registered land survey$56
Conservation fee$5
Well disclosure certificate$50
Extra copy submitted at filing$2
Deed taxPurchase price times .0033 (minimum $1.65)
Mortgage registration taxMortgage amount times .0023

Cash, check or card is accepted, and checks go to Dakota County Property Taxation & Records. A card adds a 2.49% service charge on recordings, none on copy requests.

sections.h2: What is the deed tax on a Dakota County sale?
sections.html:
The state deed tax is the purchase price multiplied by .0033, which is $330 on a $100,000 price and $1,188 on a $360,000 sale. Section 287.21 sets it at .0033 of the net consideration when the price, not counting liens that stay on the property, is above $3,000, and at $1.65 for $3,000 or less.

The tax is due when the deed is presented for recording. On a transfer worth $3,000 or less, the county asks you to enclose $1.65 and write "Total consideration for this transfer is $3,000 or less" on the deed. Above that amount an electronic certificate of real estate value is needed under section 272.115, and the certificate must be on file for the next homestead classification to apply.

sections.h2: What must a Dakota County deed contain to be accepted?
sections.html:
Dakota County follows the document standards in Minnesota Statutes section 507.093. Every document must be dated and signed, carry a complete notary acknowledgment, have the full legal description (not the tax description), attach any exhibits it references, and include a drafting statement and the filing fee. White-out is not accepted.

  • The deed tax is paid and the certificate of real estate value is complete.
  • The grantee's name and address are listed so future tax statements reach the right person.
  • Delinquent taxes are paid, and current taxes too if the parcel is being split.
  • A married seller is joined by the spouse, who signs and is acknowledged as grantor.
  • Well information is included: a certificate with the $50 fee, or one of the two statements the county prints on its recording page.
  • The $5 agricultural conservation fee is paid on transfers and mortgages.

A deed that completes a contract for deed needs a well statement signed by the buyers or a well certificate.

sections.h2: Why might the recorder return a Dakota County document?
sections.html:
The county lists the reasons it will send a document back unrecorded, and every one is avoidable with a check before you mail or bring it in.

  • Delinquent real estate tax is due on the parcel.
  • The drafting statement is missing.
  • The deed tax or mortgage registration tax is wrong.
  • The legal description is incorrect or looks questionable against county records.
  • The certificate of real estate value is missing or incomplete.
  • The mailing name and address for future tax statements is left out.
  • The notary acknowledgment is incomplete.
  • The recording fee is wrong, or well information is missing from a transfer.

Under section 272.12 the auditor must also confirm no delinquent tax exists, and the deed carries a note "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered" before the recorder can accept it. A correction document needs new signatures, new acknowledgments and a correction statement.

sections.h2: What is the difference between Abstract and Torrens land in Dakota County?
sections.html:
Minnesota has two land record systems. Most Dakota County property is Abstract, so a title company has to search the records for anything that touches the parcel when it sells. Torrens property has a Certificate of Title that serves as conclusive proof of ownership, with some exceptions, and the county charges more for Torrens work, such as $20 for each additional Torrens memorial, $46 for the first certificate canceled and issued on a transfer, and $40 for each additional certificate.

To see which system applies to a parcel, open the Property Information Search, enter the parcel ID or house number, and use the map layer icon. Owners can convert Abstract land to Torrens through land registration.

sections.h2: How big is the volume of transfers the Dakota County recorder handles?
sections.html:
The office keeps the property records for every parcel in a county of 185,931 housing units and 174,362 households. The Census Bureau counted 2,330 building permits there in 2025, and 89.0% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most addresses change hands slowly.

Dakota County was named for the Dakota bands, and the Treaty of Mendota in 1851 opened land here to settlement. Hastings, where recording happens, became the hub of the county by 1900 because of its position on the Mississippi, the St. Croix and the Vermillion River. The county seat stayed there even after the western suburbs boomed, which is why the Western and Northern Service Centers take tax payments but not recordings.

sections.h2: How can you search Dakota County records online?
sections.html:
The county's free Property Information Search shows tax, valuation and parcel data from a parcel ID, house number or address. RecordEASE is the paid tool for recorded documents, searched by legal description, grantor, grantee or document type.

Occasional users pay $5 a session, $1 per search and $2 to view a document. Subscribers pay $30 a month, $0.50 per search and $1.50 per document, and need an escrow account. Certificates of title cost $3 or $2.50 each. Veterans who recorded a discharge in the county can ask for a free DD214 copy, and most liens can be removed by filing a satisfaction, which stays on record as a permanent entry.

faqs.q: Can I record a Dakota County deed at the Western or Northern Service Center?
faqs.a: No. The county accepts property documents for recording only at the Property Taxation and Records office in the Administration Center in Hastings. You can also mail them to 1590 Highway 55, Hastings, MN 55033.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Dakota County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $46 per document, plus the $5 conservation fee on transfers, the $50 well certificate if needed, and state deed tax of .0033 times the price. A card adds 2.49%.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of real estate value in Dakota County?
faqs.a: Yes, when the price is above $3,000, you complete an electronic certificate of real estate value. For $3,000 or less, none is needed, but you enclose $1.65 and add the required statement to the deed.

faqs.q: How long until the Dakota County recorder returns my original deed?
faqs.a: The county mails originals back to the submitter within one to two weeks. Include a self-addressed stamped envelope with a mailed filing. Questions go to 651-438-4597.

faqs.q: Does Dakota County help fill out a deed form?
faqs.a: No. The county does not help complete legal forms and takes no liability for people who do it themselves. Minnesota uniform conveyance forms are on the Department of Commerce site.
